subject: Delegation playbook for air-gapped VPC DNS and TLS handoff
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: maria.gonzalez@fintechx.com, security-engineering@acme-corp.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delegation playbook for air-gapped VPC DNS and TLS handoff

Hi Maria / SecEng team,

Thanks again for walking through the private deployment requirements yesterday. Per our conversation sending a concise playbook draft and a couple of options we think will work in air-gapped VPCs where the customer retains the root CA. High-level asks up front:

- Confirm who will own the private DNS zone (FinTechX preferred?) and how you prefer delegation (private hosted zone, stub zone, or on-prem authoritative).
- Confirm CA model: customer-managed CA (preferred by compliance) vs. Redwood-assisted offline signing for temporary certs.
- Confirm secure artifact transfer method for certs/CSRs (S3 presigned, secure SFTP, or physical media for air-gapped).

Attached: proposal_v1.pdf (playbook outline), network-diagram.png.

Quick summary of the two recommended tracks:
1) Customer-managed CA (recommended): FinTechX issues private FQDN certs and uploads them into the private control plane during install. We provide CSR templates and the installation checklist.
2) Redwood-assisted offline signing: For situations where customer cannot issue certs, Redwood can provide CSR templates, receive offline-signed certs and install them. This requires out-of-band verification and an agreed short-lived intermediate.

I’d like to lock on the preferred track so we can produce the final steps and a runbook. Can we schedule a 30m sync this week?

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@fintechx.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: security-engineering@acme-corp.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delegation playbook for air-gapped VPC DNS and TLS handoff

Thanks Ava — good summary.

FinTechX policy is that we retain ownership of all private TLS material. We cannot accept Redwood-issued CAs in production; any certificates must be issued by our internal PKI. That said, we can provide pre-signed certs to your install team via an approved secure transfer. For air-gapped environments we follow two patterns today:

- Secure transfer via an internal S3 bucket with presigned URLs and time-limited keys (our preferred).
- Where S3 is not possible, we use secure removable media delivered under chain-of-custody for the install window.

Questions:
- Do you have a CSR template we can use to ensure SANs match the required FQDN list?
- What exact metadata does Redwood need from our CA (chain order, OCSP stapling preference, private key handling notes)?

Cc'ing our SecEng group — they will verify the compliance constraints. We generally prefer the Customer-managed CA track. Please send over the CSR template and a step-by-step handoff checklist.

Regards,
Maria Gonzalez
Director, Platform Security — FinTechX
maria.gonzalez@fintechx.com

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: maria.gonzalez@fintechx.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delegation playbook for air-gapped VPC DNS and TLS handoff

Maria — thanks, that clears the compliance constraint. Attached is csr_samples.txt with a couple of CSR templates (wildcard/private fqdn and per-host) and notes about SAN ordering. Below is a concise checklist for the Customer-managed CA track and a fallback option if needed.

Customer-managed CA (preferred) — high level playbook:
1) DNS ownership: FinTechX creates a private hosted zone for "internal.redwood.fintechx" (example) or delegates a subdomain to Redwood as a stub. We recommend delegation to reduce glue changes on your authoritative servers.
2) CSR generation: FinTechX generates CSRs using the provided templates. Include the complete chain (root -> intermediate) in PEM.
3) Secure transfer: upload cert bundle + chain to the agreed S3 presigned URL. For air-gapped, physically transfer the bundle using approved media (chain-of-custody).
4) Install: Redwood operator runs an offline installer that consumes the bundle and installs the certs on the private control plane and edge proxies.
5) mTLS: If you want mutual TLS between edge proxy and backend, include client certs in the bundle.
6) Rotation & revocation: we will provide a rotation window (30–90 days depending on TTL) and an emergency revocation checklist.

Fallback (Redwood-assisted offline signing):
- We provide CSR templates and an offline signing process. Customer signs with internal CA and returns certs. Redwood will not store private keys; keys must be generated and retained by the customer.

Technical notes:
- DNS: prefer private hosted zone delegation or split-horizon. Avoid /etc/hosts or local resolver hacks. TTLs should be low during rollout (60s–300s) to avoid caching issues.
- Probe/health checks: internal health checks rely on FQDNs; ensure internal DNS resolves from all cluster nodes.
- K8s ingress TLS: use secret-based certs (k8s TLS secret). Operator will reference those secrets during rollout.

I’ll prepare a formal playbook doc and a one-page runbook for your SecOps team. Any constraints on TTL or rotation windows we should pre-seed?

Best,
Ava

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delegation playbook for air-gapped VPC DNS and TLS handoff

Adding a few operational points from the infra side (short bullets):

- Key handling: If customer wants us to perform installation, we must receive certs without private keys. Private keys must be generated and kept by customer; installer accepts cert PEM + chain only.
- Rotation: document the operator steps to swap k8s secrets, restart proxy pods in a graceful rolling update, and validate chain with curl --cacert.
- Revocation: since internal PKIs sometimes lack OCSP, include a manual revocation play (remove cert + fallback route to HTTP over internal network for emergency maintenance).
- Sample proxy config: I sketched a minimal haproxy/stunnel example in the attached stunnel-haproxy-example.conf — it shows TLS termination on the edge proxy and mTLS to backend services.
- DNS troubleshooting: include dig + tcpdump sample commands; suggest adding a short checklist for split-horizon test cases (resolver order, search domains, /etc/resolv.conf expectations).

If we land on Customer-managed CA the next action item is: Ava to produce the final playbook doc and a one-page runbook for SecOps. I can convert my proxy snippets into repo-ready manifests.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Delegation playbook for air-gapped VPC DNS and TLS handoff

Ava / team — we agree to the Customer-managed CA track. Next steps from FinTechX:

1) We will generate the cert bundles and provide them via our S3 presigned URLs.
2) Expect a single bundle per environment (dev/stage/prod).
3) Rotation window: we prefer 90 days; we will accept 30 days for emergency rotation if documented.
4) Please provide the formal playbook + runbook and the exact CSR template by EOD Thursday (2027-03-25).

Let's schedule a 30m call to walk through the runbook and the transfer method tomorrow or Wednesday. Proposed times: 10:00–12:00 PST Tue/Wed. Send a calendar invite and include the S3 presigned URL template we should use.

Thanks,
Maria
